issues: Frame 2 re-registers or redraws much of the helmet and body; the difference panels light up the crown, brim, sides, face, and lower silhouette instead of isolating the feet.

Frame 1's left step forms a long diagonal orange wedge, while frame 2's right step forms a larger stair-stepped extension; the alternating poses are not cleanly balanced.
The walk is readable, but the broad whole-sprite changes make the loop lurch instead of delivering the economical foot swap expected from a Capcom NES enemy.
fixes: Copy the helmet from frame 1 into frame 2 at exactly the same coordinates, including the crown, black rim, brim, and black helmet detail.
Keep the eyes, white face clusters, and central black body pixels identical in both frames; confine animation to the bottom few rows.
Redraw frame 1's left foot as a compact two- or three-cluster extension instead of the long diagonal orange connection into the torso.
Shorten frame 2's right orange wedge and make its stepped silhouette match the visual weight of frame 1's extended foot.
Use one fixed body anchor for both frames and alternate only the forward toe and rear tucked foot, with a deliberate one-pixel bob only if it is consistently applied.

fixes: Align frame 2's helmet crown, side slopes, brim, and interior helmet marks exactly to frame 1 so those pixels remain unchanged.
Keep the eye and central body clusters at identical coordinates in both frames; animate only the pixels below the body.
In frame 1, shorten the left orange extension and define a compact two- or three-pixel foot with a clear flat contact edge.
In frame 2, apply the same compact construction to the right foot, swapping only the leading and trailing foot clusters for the loop.

issues: Frame 2 shifts the helmet, face, and body laterally instead of limiting the change to the stepping feet; the extensive helmet-edge changes in both difference panels make the loop visibly jitter.

fixes: In frame 2, align the helmet brim, crown, highlight, eyes, and round body exactly to frame 1 so those pixels remain unchanged.
Redraw only the bottom two or three pixel rows in frame 2: retract frame 1's leading toe and extend the opposite foot by one pixel to create the alternate step.
Keep the body's center and helmet silhouette fixed across the loop; if a weight shift is desired, change only one or two contact pixels beneath the body rather than translating the upper sprite.
Check the revised difference row: magenta should be concentrated around the feet, with at most a tiny deliberate body bob and no changes around the helmet perimeter.

issues: Frames 1 and 2 clearly alternate the feet, but the body shifts laterally enough that the loop reads as a side-to-side snap rather than a stable walk.

fixes: Keep the helmet, its highlight, cross detail, brim, and outer contour pixel-identical in both frames.
Lock the eyes and central body to one anchor position; animate only the lowest leg and foot rows, with at most a one-pixel body bob.
Redraw frame 2's right foot to match the length and cluster weight of frame 1's extended left foot.
Reduce the changed pixels under the brim by preserving the same black torso and white eye clusters in both frames.
Use a compact two-pose cycle: one foot extends by one or two pixels while the opposite foot retracts, then swap those exact clusters in frame 2.

issues: Frame 2 does alternate the extended foot, so the walk reads, but the difference row shows changes across the helmet crown, sloped sides, brim, and face instead of being confined mainly to the legs.
